title: Large language models underestimate and partly misrepresent cultural variation in everyday norms

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM estimates of the social appropriateness of everyday behaviors across 90 societies against human survey data (Global Study of Everyday Norms) to assess whether models capture cross-cultural variations, underestimate societal differences, or default to Western/US norms when unprompted.
Correlating the models' estimation errors of societal norms with the Human Development Index (HDI) of each society to determine if LLM accuracy is higher for more economically developed countries.

Evaluating if prompting models in a society's local survey language, rather than English, improves the accuracy of cultural differentiation and reduces the underestimation of cross-cultural variation.
